introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.lead: Bayrust is the launcher, AI chat, notes and settings app documented here, rebuilt from the shipped 2.8.2 frontend. These docs cover its foundations, components, blocks, window templates and every captured flow.
introduction.md:
## What's in the system

Everything on these pages is the app itself: its stylesheets, tokens, icon sprite, fonts and images, and its own components and windows rendered live from their markup. Nothing is redrawn and nothing is a screenshot. Components Bayrust doesn't ship are composed from its own parts and labelled as such.

- **Foundations:** colour, typography, spacing, radius, elevation and materials, motion, iconography, logo and window layout. Each value is a CSS variable with a Dark and a Light value.
- **Components:** 80 documented components, listed A–Z. Each example is the component's own rendered markup, previewed with the shipped stylesheets.
- **Blocks:** 12 larger pieces of UI (search bar, list, action bar, sidebars, composer, onboarding cards), shown as native renders with their markup.
- **Templates:** the window layouts: default, compact and full screen.
- **Flows:** 102 states across 8 flows, from onboarding to Send Feedback, rendered natively at measured window sizes.

## Sources

| Output | Count |
|---|---|
| Named components in the frontend | 1,783 |
| Components with recovered props | 1,241 |
| CSS variables (Dark + Light) | 467 |
| Icon sprite symbols | 730 |
| Shipped stylesheets | 158 |
| Flow states | 102 |

## Conventions

- **Theme.** Previews follow the docs theme switch: Bayrust Dark or Bayrust Light.
- **Accent.** The app uses the macOS accent colour when the host provides it (`--accent: var(--color-system-accent, var(--theme-accent))`). Previews use this Mac's: Blue, `#007AFF`.
- **Size.** All sizes are at Interface Size 100% (`--zoom: 1`). Every space, icon and font token scales with `--spx`.

installation.title: Installation
installation.lead: Install the design system as a package, or run the live app and these docs from the repository.
installation.md:
## Install the package

```install
@krackedui/bayrust
```

It's public on npm under the `@krackedui` scope: `npm install`, `pnpm add` or `yarn add` works with no login.

The package carries the images the components load, so icons, empty states and illustrations render as they do in
the app. Video is the one thing left out: the two shipped `.mp4` files are not published.

| Import | What it is |
|---|---|
| `@krackedui/bayrust/css` | The shipped component styles, both themes and their fonts |
| `@krackedui/bayrust` | Design tokens (typed), the CSS-module class names of the shipped styles, icon names, the root's attributes |
| `@krackedui/bayrust/react` | `ThemeRoot`, `Icon`, and `Bayrust`, which runs a shipped component inside your React app |
| `@krackedui/bayrust/components` | `loadBayrust()`: every shipped component by name, without React of your own |
| `@krackedui/bayrust/vite` | Serves and bundles the files the components and icons load at runtime |
| `@krackedui/bayrust/tokens.css`, `tokens.json`, `icons/*.svg` | Tokens as CSS and JSON, and the 730 icons as files |

## Use it

Add the Vite plugin, which serves the shipped components' runtime at `/bayrust/` and copies it into your build:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import bayrust from '@krackedui/bayrust/vite';

export default { plugins: [bayrust()] };
```

Then wrap your UI in a theme root and use the components:

```tsx
import '@krackedui/bayrust/css';
import { ThemeRoot, Icon, Bayrust } from '@krackedui/bayrust/react';

export function Toolbar() {
  return (
    <ThemeRoot theme="dark">
      <Icon name="magnifying-glass" />
      <Bayrust component="Button" props={{ text: 'Run Script', variant: 'secondary', onClick: () => run() }} />
    </ThemeRoot>
  );
}
```

`Bayrust` mounts the shipped component with the React it was built with, inside yours; its props, including event handlers, are passed as given. The shipped styles also work with your own markup through the class names:

```tsx
import { classes } from '@krackedui/bayrust';

<button className={classes['action-button'].button}>Copy</button>;
```

Without Vite (Next.js and others), copy the runtime into your public folder once, and the default `/bayrust/` finds it:

```bash
npx bayrust copy public/bayrust
```

Without React of your own:

```ts
import { loadBayrust } from '@krackedui/bayrust/components';

const ui = await loadBayrust();
const Toggle = await ui.get('Toggle');
ui.render(document.querySelector('#settings'), ui.h(Toggle, { checked: true }));
```

## The live app

The harness serves the shipped frontend, runs the app's own backend in a sandbox, and answers the native host's calls.

```bash
node harness/server.mjs
```

| URL | Window |
|---|---|
| `http://localhost:4317/main-window.html` | Launcher, 750 × 475 |
| `http://localhost:4317/main-window.html?windowMode=compact` | Launcher, compact |
| `http://localhost:4317/welcome-window.html?variant=standard` | Onboarding, 1280 × 760 |
| `http://localhost:4317/settings-window.html` | Settings, 800 × 786 |
| `http://localhost:4317/ai-chat-window.html` | AI Chat, 750 × 600 |
| `http://localhost:4317/notes-window.html` | Notes, 396 wide |
| `http://localhost:4317/theme-studio-window.html` | Theme Studio, 1370 × 570 |
| `http://localhost:4317/feedback-window.html` | Send Feedback, 420 × 714 |

Add `?brand=original` to any window to turn the Bayrust rename off.

## The docs

```bash
cd design-system/docs
npm install
npm run content
npm run dev
```

`npm run content` rebuilds `src/content/content.json` and `public/ds/` from the extraction outputs.

color.title: Color
color.lead: Thirteen theme base colours, each with alpha steps, and semantic text, border and surface tokens built from them.
color.md:
## How colour is built

The theme sets thirteen base colours on `.active-theme`: `--bg`, `--bg-secondary`, `--fg`, `--theme-accent`, `--selection`, `--loader` and the seven hues. Every other colour is derived from these:

- **Alpha steps.** `.theme-root` defines `-0`, `-5`, `-10`, `-20`, `-40`, `-60` and `-80` for each base colour, as `rgb(from var(--fg) r g b / 60%)`.
- **Semantic tokens.** Text, border and surface tokens point at those steps, for example `--color-text-secondary: var(--fg-60)`.
- **Accent.** `--accent: var(--color-system-accent, var(--theme-accent))`. When the host provides the macOS accent colour, it wins over the theme's.
- **Window.** The window backdrop is `linear-gradient(to bottom, var(--color-window-bg), var(--color-window-bg-secondary))` over the native glass material.

The palette above lists the 10% and 20% steps; the other steps follow the same formula.

typography.title: Typography
typography.lead: InterVariable for the interface and JetBrains Mono for code, in fifteen named text styles.
typography.md:
## Typefaces

| Family | Files | Use |
|---|---|---|
| InterVariable | `InterVariable.woff2`, `InterVariable-Italic.woff2` (weights 100–900) | Interface text |
| JetBrainsMono | `JetBrainsMono-Regular.woff2` | Code, shortcuts and numbers in mono styles |

Root settings: `font-feature-settings: "liga" 1, "calt" 1, "kern" 1, "ss03" 1`, `font-synthesis: none`, `font-optical-sizing: none`. On macOS, `-webkit-font-smoothing: subpixel-antialiased` and `font-family: InterVariable, system-ui, sans-serif`. Line height is left at the browser default.

## Text colours

`text` takes a `color` prop: `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `quaternary`, `disabled`, `link`, `accent`, `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `purple`, `magenta` (and `inherit`). Each maps to a `--color-text-*` token or a hue.

## Font sizes

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `--font-size-8` | 8px |
| `--font-size-11` | 11px |
| `--font-size-13` | 13px |
| `--font-size-16` | 16px |
| `--font-size-18` | 18px |
| `--font-size-24` | 24px |

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.lead: Eleven spacing steps and four icon sizes, all scaled by Interface Size.
spacing.md:
## Scaling

Space, icon and font tokens are `round(calc(n * var(--spx)), 1px)` with `--spx: calc(1px * var(--zoom, 1))`. `--zoom` follows the Interface Size setting (Settings › General), so the whole UI scales on whole pixels.

## Icon sizes

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `--icon-12` | 12px |
| `--icon-16` | 16px |
| `--icon-22` | 22px |
| `--icon-32` | 32px |
| `--icon-size` |  |
| `--icon-badge-icon-size` |  |

radius.title: Radius
radius.lead: Corner radii from 2 px to the window radius, which depends on the macOS version.
radius.md:
## Window radius

`--radius-window` is `--radius-window-macos-27` (20 px) on macOS 27 and `--radius-window-macos-26` (26 px) on macOS 26. On Windows it is 8 px.

## Concentric corners

The radius classes also set `--radius-closest`, so nested elements can use the radius of their nearest rounded parent.

elevation.title: Elevation & materials
elevation.lead: Panels float on a layered shadow over native glass; blurs come in four steps.
elevation.md:
## Materials

Windows are native `NSGlassEffectView` windows. The web content draws its backdrop with WebKit's `-apple-visual-effect: -apple-system-glass-material-media-controls`, which needs the host's `useSystemAppearance`, and a translucent gradient on top (`.theme-root:before`).

Child panels (the action panel, menus) are separate native windows opened with `window.open()`, sized to their content.

## Blur

| Token | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| `--blur-1` | 6px | 15px |
| `--blur-2` | 12px | 35px |
| `--blur-3` | 24px | 60px |
| `--blur-4` | 36px | 120px |

iconography.title: Iconography
iconography.lead: 730 icons from the shipped sprite, drawn on a 16 × 16 grid.
iconography.md:
## Using icons

The UI references a symbol with `<use href="ipc://raycast-sprite/<name>#s">`; the host serves the symbol from the sprite. Sizes come from `--icon-12`, `--icon-16`, `--icon-22` and `--icon-32`, and colour from `currentColor`.

Names ending in `-1px` are thin-stroke variants; names ending in `-20` are drawn for 20 px. `brand-*` icons are third-party marks.

logo.title: Logo
logo.lead: The mark in its three flavors, and the app icons from the asset catalog.
logo.md:
## Flavors

`Logo` takes `flavor`: `Production` fills with `--red`; `Internal` and `Development` fill with a two-stop gradient (`--purple` → `--blue`, and `--logo-color1-development` → `--yellow`).

## App icons

The app icons are the PNG renditions in `Assets.car`: Production, Internal, Development and RayConfig.

## Name

The artwork is unchanged. Only the displayed name is Bayrust.

layout.title: Layout
layout.lead: Window sizes, header and footer heights, split views, and how windows fill the screen.
layout.md:
## Windows

| Window | Size (pt) | Source | Traffic lights |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launcher | 750 × 475 | CSS tokens `--main-window-width`, `--main-window-expanded-height`; measured | No |
| Launcher, compact | 750 × 64 | `--main-window-header-height` (64 on macOS) | No |
| Onboarding | 1280 × 760 | Measured | Yes |
| Pro walkthrough | 1280 × 760 (712 on feature pages) | Code | Yes |
| AI Chat | 750 × 600 | Saved window frame | Yes |
| Settings | 800 × 786 | Measured | Yes |
| Notes | 396 wide, height follows the note (830 for the welcome note) | Measured | No |
| Theme Studio | 1370 × 570 | Measured | Yes |
| Send Feedback | 420 × 714 | Measured | Yes |
| Any window, full screen | 1710 × 1107 (this Mac’s built-in display) | Measured | — |

## Header and footer

| Token | macOS | Elsewhere |
|---|---|---|
| `--main-window-header-height` | 64 | 66 |
| `--main-window-footer-height` | 44 (`--default-window-footer-height`) | 42 |
| `--default-window-header-height` | 52 | 52 (Windows: `--space-40`) |
| `--notes-window-footer-height` | 48 on macOS 27 | 52 |
| `--ai-chat-window-header-height` | 52 (44 on macOS 26) | 52 |

## Compact and full screen

The launcher has two window modes (Settings › General › Window Mode): **Default** opens at 750 × 475 with root search results; **Compact** opens as the 64 pt search bar alone and expands once you type. Windows with traffic lights can also fill the screen. Their content stretches and keeps the same tokens. See [Templates](/templates-launcher) for each window in each mode.

#### Variants and states

| Module | Selector | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `settings-ui` | `data-align` | `center`, `start` |
| `settings-ui` | `data-highlight` | `(present)` |
| `settings-ui` | `data-inline` | `true` |
| `settings-ui` | `data-settings-description` | `(present)` |
| `settings-ui` | `data-settings-accessory` | `(present)` |
| `settings-ui` | `data-variant` | `default` |
| `settings-ui` | `:focus` | — |
| `settings-ui` | `:focus-visible` | — |
| `settings-ui` | `:active` | — |

| `settings-ui` | `data-has-padding-top` | `false` |
| `settings-ui` | `data-has-padding-bottom` | `false` |

#### Anatomy

| CSS module | Parts |

| `settings-ui` | `accessory`, `column`, `extensionHeaderButtons`, `extensionIntro`, `extensionIntroDescription`, `extensionIntroDescriptionContainer`, `extensionIntroIcon`, `extensionIntroTitle`, `interactiveItem`, `interactiveItemIcon`, `interactiveItemText`, `interactiveItemTextColumn`, `linkIcon`, `root`, `row`, `rowLeft` |

#### Accessibility

Native elements: `<button>` ×10. Roles: `alert` ×5, `status` ×5. ARIA attributes: `aria-label` ×10, `aria-hidden` ×3.

states.lead: Hover, focus, active, selected, disabled, open, checked, error and read-only, as the stylesheets define them.
states.md:
## How states are expressed

Components set state as attributes, and the stylesheets style the attributes: `data-state="hover|pressed|focus|open"` on buttons, `data-selected` on list items, `data-variant="error"` on fields, plus native `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:active` and `:disabled`. design-tokens.title: Design tokens
design-tokens.lead: 467 CSS variables, resolved for Bayrust Dark and Bayrust Light.
design-tokens.md:
## How tokens work

Every value in the interface is a CSS variable. Some are fixed (`--radius-8: 8px`), some are built from others (`--color-text-secondary: var(--fg-60)`), and some scale with Interface Size (`--space-12: round(calc(12 * var(--spx)), 1px)`).

- **Theme base.** Thirteen colours come from the theme and are set at runtime on `.active-theme`. Everything else in colour derives from them.
- **Scale.** `--spx` is `calc(1px * var(--zoom, 1))`; space, icon and font-size tokens multiply it and round to whole pixels.
- **Platform.** `[macos]`, `[macos="26"]`, `[macos="27"]` and `[windows]` on the root swap platform values (window radius, blur, header heights).

## Families

| Family | Tokens | Example |
|---|---|---|
| typography | 11 | `--font-weight-400` |
| radius | 15 | `--radius-2` |
| blur | 4 | `--blur-1` |
| motion | 7 | `--easing-ease-out-expo` |
| other | 214 | `--spx` |
| icon-size | 6 | `--icon-12` |
| space | 11 | `--space-2` |
| shadow | 4 | `--shadow-panel-border` |
| window | 16 | `--window-border-offset` |
| color.palette | 104 | `--bg-0` |
| color.semantic | 35 | `--red-contrast` |
| color.surface | 15 | `--color-window-base` |
| color.other | 9 | `--color-fg-max` |

| color.border | 8 | `--color-border-primary` |

| `design-system/tokens/tokens.css` | The resolved values as CSS, one block per theme |

breakpoints.title: Breakpoints
breakpoints.lead: The media and container queries in the shipped stylesheets, and what they style.
breakpoints.md:
## Viewport queries

Windows have fixed or measured sizes, so most of the UI has no breakpoints. The onboarding (Welcome) window is the exception: its steps change layout at 801 px wide and 600 px tall.

responsive-design.title: Responsive design
responsive-design.lead: How the interface adapts: Interface Size, window modes, full screen and resizable windows.
responsive-design.md:
## Interface Size

Settings › General › Interface Size sets `--zoom` on the root, and every space, icon and font-size token scales with it, rounded to whole pixels.

| Option | --zoom |
|---|---|
| Default | 1 |
| Large | 1.1 |
| Larger | 1.2 |

The step is 0.1 and the maximum 1.2. AI Chat and Notes have their own content zoom (`ZoomControls`, Reset / − / %).

## Window modes

The launcher opens **Default** (750 × 475, results shown) or **Compact** (the 64 pt search bar alone, expanding as you type). See [Launcher](/templates-launcher).

## Full screen

Windows with traffic lights (Settings, AI Chat, Notes, Theme Studio, Send Feedback) can fill the screen. Their content stretches; tokens stay the same. Each template page shows the full-screen render.

## Content-driven height

Notes sizes its window to the note's height until it's resized by hand ("Enable Window Auto-Sizing" restores it).

## Reduced motion

38 rules apply under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. See [Breakpoints](/breakpoints) for the queries.

product-icons.title: Product icons
product-icons.lead: 226 product icons: 193 commands, 27 extensions and 6 apps, at 44 and 108 points.
product-icons.md: ## What these are Every command, extension and app has an icon of its own: a rounded square with a gradient and a glyph, drawn as artwork. They are the product icons, as distinct from the interface icons on [Iconography](/iconography), which are monochrome and take their colour from the text around them. These are raster, at two sizes — 44 points for lists and menus, 108 for larger surfaces. ## Using one Click an icon to copy its path. From the package the same files sit under the runtime the Vite plugin serves: ```tsx ``` The file name carries the build hash, so it changes when the app is rebuilt; copy it from here rather than typing it.

gradients.title: Gradients
gradients.lead: The window gradient, gradient borders, glows and fades.
gradients.md:
## Window

`.theme-root:before` paints `linear-gradient(to bottom, var(--color-window-bg), var(--color-window-bg-secondary))` over the glass: the theme's background and secondary background at 40%.

## Gradient border

`GradientBorder` draws a conic or linear gradient around its parent (`data-type`, `data-animated`), used by standout buttons and badges. See [Fancy Button](/button#fancy-button).

## Masks and fills

Most gradients in Bayrust are masks, not colours: they fade content out at the edges of lists, scroll areas and previews. Masks are shown here applied to the primary text colour; fills are shown as they are.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.lead: What the app provides: contrast improvement, focus rings, reduced motion and transparency, and semantic markup.
accessibility.md:
## Contrast

The contrast-improvement feature adjusts hue tokens for legibility: `--red-contrast`, `--red-on-tint-10`, `--red-on-tint-20` and the same for each hue. With `[contrast-disabled]` on the root they fall back to the plain hue. (Internal command: "Toggle Contrast Improvement".)

## Focus

`--focus-ring: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--color-border-focus-ring)`, 2 px on macOS. Controls style `:focus-visible`; see [Interaction states](/states).

## Motion and transparency

38 rules respond to `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. `.theme-root.no-transparency` swaps the translucent backdrop for an opaque one on Windows.

## Keyboard

Every action has a keyboard path: ⌘K opens the Action Panel from any item, and the action bar shows each action's shortcut. See [Keyboard Shortcut](/keyboard-shortcut).

dark-mode.title: Dark mode
dark-mode.lead: Light and dark appearance, following the system or set per appearance.
dark-mode.md:
## How it works

The root gets `dark` or `light` and the window's `.theme-root` takes `color-scheme: dark` or `light`. `--color-window-base` is `#262626` in dark and `#fff` in light; `--color-fg-max` and `--color-bg-max` swap.

## Settings

Settings › General: **Follow System Appearance**, and a **Dark Theme** and a **Light Theme** used for each appearance (Bayrust Dark and Bayrust Light by default).

## In these docs

Every live specimen follows the docs theme switch: try any component page in both. Colour tokens list both values on [Color](/color).

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.lead: What these docs were built from, and when.
changelog.md:
## 2026-10-22

- The Illustrations and Imagery galleries are gone, and the site
  carries only the images the component and window markup references. Both checklist items now read
  "In Bayrust, not published".
- The two shipped `.mp4` files are left out of the site and the package.
- `@krackedui/bayrust` is public on npm, and its runtime carries code, styles, fonts and SVG only.

## 2026-10-21 (later)

- Components are grouped into 32 families (Button holds every kind of button, Input every kind of input…), with each checklist item a section.
- Every preview is live: components, Bayrust's playground sections, live views and dialogs, and whole windows (flows, templates, blocks) rendered from their own markup. No screenshots remain.
- Previews follow Bayrust's playground: components straight on the canvas at their real size, with Variant/source annotations.
- The sandbox runs as a Pro trial account (the app's own auth-override shape), so Pro screens are documented: Account, AI sub-pages, Cloud Sync, automations.
- Components Bayrust doesn't ship are composed from its own primitives and tokens, and labelled.
- New live captures: Start Focus Session (duration picker, block list), Search AI Commands (master-detail layout), legacy password form, crash view, Dictation activity graph.

## 2026-10-21

- Components follow the design-system checklist, one page each, A–Z, with [Coverage](/coverage) for every item.
- New specimen sources: Bayrust's own component playground (68 components), internal test views, live dialogs and the colour picker, and component instances from all 94 captured states.
- New foundation pages: design tokens, sizing, breakpoints, responsive design, illustrations, imagery, shadows, borders, opacity, gradients, animation, transitions, accessibility, themes, dark mode and interaction states.
- Full-screen renders at the whole display (1710 × 1107).
- The docs take the look of Bayrust's own playground.

## 2026-10-20

- App renamed Bayrust (display layer), all 94 flow states re-rendered natively.
- Docs site built on the Open Figment docs app: foundations, components, blocks, templates and flows.
- Token extraction fixed for non-colour tokens (shadows, focus ring).

## Source

Everything is extracted from the shipped macOS app at version 2.8.2, nothing is drawn or estimated. Module names on each page carry the shipped file's hash, which identifies the exact build.
